title: Short demo of my 2D pixel art raising sim, made solo after work
author: chwh_dev
selftext:
You can go to the exchange and invest in stocks through a monster who is the archmage's familiar, save up money with part-time jobs, or head to the gate and clear dungeons for rewards. There are many ways to get rich in a fantasy world, after all.

In the full version, I'm planning for you to raise your character for about 10 years and see what kind of rich person they become in the ending. If it ever gets released, that is. It's still in development, so only the first year is open for now. It should be about 10 minutes of play.

Play link: [https://chwh.app/?src=reddit-en](https://chwh.app/?src=reddit-en)

Just open it in your browser and play comfortably. It's the same game on phone, tablet and desktop, but I've matched the resolution & UI for each. That said, since I'm developing it in Korean, there are still a few broken parts.



I'd really appreciate any feedback if you have the time. And cheers to everyone grinding away and burning tokens, thanks to the every-other-day Codex resets(tibo 28d) over the past two weeks. I've got 20% of my Claude usage left, so I'll work hard through tomorrow and then I'd like to get a good rest the day after. I'm not young anymore, and I can feel my health getting worse. I tried to burn through my Astra quota by giving it a big batch of mass production, but all it burned was tokens, and the results were dog crap.

  
I wanted to make the kind of game I loved as a kid, so when Opus 5.5 and Astra came out, I jumped right on them.

I've been doing game dev for about 2 months now. The game I spent the first month on turned out so bad that I scrapped it, and thanks to Tibo's Codex reset challenge I started over with this one.

I'm a newbie whose skills aren't good enough to avoid 3D art or AI slop. So instead, I decided to make a classic pixel art game that smells like an old man.

I've been making it while picking out well-reviewed tools and trying out subscriptions to them. Keeping the art tone consistent and getting results that match what's in my head is still hard. I'm figuring it out little by little, but I'm still such a newbie that I can't get good results unless I use max effort.

comments.author: KS-Wolf-1978
comments.body:
I see both big pixels and nice anime style HD art.

Decide on one.

My vote goes for HD art (i'm old enough to remember not just pixels, but also binary color).

replies.author: chwh_dev
replies.body: Thanks for calling the anime style nice! I guess big pixels might not be for most people, or they might just not match my game. Thanks for the feedback!

replies.author: YoungandPregnant
replies.body: anecdotally, I like the mix up of styles.

replies.author: chwh_dev
replies.body: Thanks for your input! I'm developing this alone without much experience, so feedback really helps. Even if I stick with pixels, I'll work on it so players can feel the effort that went into it. Have a good day!

replies.author: mermaidreefer
replies.body: I’m gonna have to say I love the combined style. I understand it not being people’s cup of tea, but it’s mine.

replies.author: chwh_dev
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback! I tried to copy the style of games I remember, but I did it without much thought, so I think it looked awkward and strange to people. I'll work on making the art more polished and more my own. Thank you!

replies.author: CrowdGoesWildWoooo
replies.body: Yeah this is what gets your game called AI slop, like you see many different styles, but the way it’s put feels like someone who doesn’t know what they are doing as opposed to something that is intentional.

replies.author: chwh_dev
replies.body: I'll think more about the feedback on consistency and originality. Thank you!

comments.author: bingewavecinema
comments.body: I think either you need to make the character sharper or dull the background a bit. The background looks realistic,the characters are obviously pixel. It kind of clashes instead of flowing.

replies.author: chwh_dev
replies.body: A lot of people are saying the same thing, so I should think about a different direction. Thanks for the feedback!

comments.author: Salty_Device2368
comments.body: Could you maybe consider something else than Pixel Art? Nothing against it, but every single game here is pixel art.

replies.author: chwh_dev
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback! I'm still inexperienced, so my view on art is pretty narrow. I'll keep studying.

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body: not an attack but does every use the exact same image model , reference image and prompt?

replies.author: chwh_dev
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback! I'll try to use more of my own imagination.

replies.author: chwh_dev
replies.body: This is exactly the advice a beginner like me needs. Thank you! I'll think more about what kind of artwork could really bring the concept to life.

comments.author: thetinytrex
comments.body: I'm seeing a lot of different styles and it's kind of jarring. Even though this is an aigamedev sub, I think our goal is to make our games not feel and look like AI games and I see a lot of the style of the chatgpt standard pixel style that I get whenever I prompt it for pixel art. I personally like PixelLab but it requires a lot of clean-up if you want to check that out. I'm liking what I get way more than what Opus can draw or Codex will generate. A good tip is to stick with a color palette too as it will make the whole game feel more cohesive. You can go to lospec for them, all free.

replies.author: chwh_dev
replies.body: Thanks for the tips on color palettes and PixelLab! I'll look into them more.

comments.author: Ok_Extension_9790
comments.body: Hey men, good work. How do you create those 2D sprites? AI help you with that?

replies.author: chwh_dev
replies.body: Thanks! I used GPT's image model. People's feedback here is spot on, it seems the results look too similar to everyone else's.
